items.item: A read that starts after a write completes may still legally return the old value under sequential consistency, something linearizability forbids outright.

items.item: Causal consistency requires only that causally related operations, by happens-before, appear in the same order everywhere; concurrent operations may be seen in different orders by different processes.

at.step: Reveal: causal consistency orders only cause and effect

items.item: In the chat example, every participant observes the question before either answer, since answering causally depends on reading it, while the two concurrent answers may be observed in either order.

items.item: Read-your-writes requires that a process's own subsequent read observe the effects of its own prior write, and says nothing about what other processes observe.

items.item: Monotonic reads requires that a later read by the same process never observe a state older than an earlier read by that same process.

at.step: Reveal: four session guarantees, each one breakable alone

items.item: Monotonic writes requires that if the same process performs write w1 then w2, every process that observes w2 has already observed w1.

at.step: Reveal: four session guarantees, each one breakable alone

items.item: Writes-follow-reads requires that a write issued after a read that observed some prior write becomes visible everywhere only after that prior write.

at.step: Reveal: four session guarantees, each one breakable alone

items.item: None of the four session guarantees is stronger than any other; each can fail independently while the other three continue to hold.

items.item: This topic does not assert that the four session guarantees together amount to causal consistency; that equivalence needs reading Terry et al. and the later literature on how the four combine, which was not independently verified here.

at.step: Reveal: what this doesn't claim

items.item: Sequential consistency and linearizability both require giving up availability during a partition, which is why neither is reachable for a store that promises to always answer, leaving causal consistency as the strongest remaining option.
